title: Urim and Thummim
lead: Objects kept in the high priest's breastpiece through which Israel sought God's decisions, probably a kind of sacred lot (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21; 1 Samuel 14:41; 28:6). Their use fades after David's time, and by the return from exile no priest had them (Ezra 2:63).

sections.h: Urim and Thummim across the Bible
sections.b: Exodus 28:30 and Leviticus 8:8 put them into the high priest's breastpiece. Numbers 27:21 says Joshua will receive God's decisions through Eleazar and the Urim. Moses' blessing gives them to Levi (Deuteronomy 33:8). Saul seeks a decision through them, and the longer Greek text of 1 Samuel 14:41 shows them working as two lots, "Urim" for one answer and "Thummim" for the other. When God will not answer Saul "whether through dreams, through the Urim or through the prophets" (1 Samuel 28:6), it marks his abandonment. After the exile no priest can consult them, so questions are put off "until a priest arises with Urim and Thummim" (Ezra 2:63; Nehemiah 7:65).
